title: Atomic prefill checkpointing to prevent interleaved kernel race during multi-stream decode
creator: Diego Morales
description: Background: Multi-stream decode uses concurrent CUDA streams and CUDA Graph capture/replay to get low-latency, high-throughput token generation. We observed non-deterministic token corruption and KV cache divergence in heavy mixed-workload clusters (short/long context mixes) caused by interleaved kernel launches during prefill->decode transitions and partial graph recapture. Problem: When prefill sequences execute on multiple streams, current graph capture heuristics allow segments to be captured with overlapping kernel bindings. During replay, race windows permit a downstream decode stream to start replaying a captured graph while an upstream stream is still finalizing prefill writes to shared KV memory regions. That manifests as: - token-level hallucinations in ~0.2% of requests under stress - occasional KV cache rollback detected by post-request validation - rare segfaults for fused-attention kernels when prefill stride assumptions are violated Goal: Implement an atomic checkpointing mechanism for prefill capture and a lightweight journaled replay validator to ensure capture/replay correctness without regressing p50 latency by more than 3% or p99 by more than 7% in typical production mixes.
acceptance_criteria: Prefill checkpointing prevents inter-stream races: under mixed short/long context synthetic load we observe zero KV divergence incidents across 1M generated tokens
Post-replay checksum validation detects and aborts corrupted replays with a safe fallback to non-graph decode
End-to-end p50 latency regression <= 3% and p99 <= 7% versus current baseline on runtime-2.2 perf harness
New telemetry events emitted for checkpoint creation, replay-validated, and replay-abort (available in Console traces)
Design and implementation reviewed by runtime and infra leads (approvals recorded in PR and Confluence)
implementation_notes: Add per-graph 'checkpoint token' written atomically at end of prefill capture. Implementation uses a 64-bit monotonically increasing sequence id stored with KV metadata and CUDA unified memory fence to guarantee visibility across streams.

Introduce 'journaled segments' concept: when capturing a multi-segment graph, write lightweight header entries for segment offsets + checksum into a small GPU-resident journal buffer that is part of capture state.

On replay, validate checkpoint token + segment checksums before starting token decode. If validation fails, fall back to immediate non-graph decode path for that request and emit a 'replay-abort' trace.

Kernel-binding changes: reserve conservative kernel selection for first two prefill iterations to avoid transient fusion assumptions that cause different register allocation across captures. This is an opt-in flag for canary builds to measure overhead.
Keep journal and checkpointing disabled by default for lightweight captures; enable via runtime config per-customer or per-model during rollout.

Memory overhead: journal buffer sized at O(number_of_segments * 32 bytes). For typical sequences this is <4KB per graph instance. Track GPU-resident allocation with CompactAllocator to avoid fragmentation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for journal write/read and atomic checkpoint update under synthetic concurrency (gtest).
Integrated CI job that spins up multi-stream harness (short/long context mix) with seeded RNG to try to reproduce previous divergence; assert no divergence in 100k runs.
Canary staged rollout: enable journaled checkpointing for 5% of requests in internal dev cluster, monitor KV divergence, token-level diffs, and throughput for 48h.
Perf regression tests: runtime-2.2 harness with microbench scripts for p50/p90/p99 and end-to-end token costs. Thresholds per acceptance criteria.
Chaos test: prefill capture interrupts (preemption) simulated and ensure replay abort path and fallback decode succeed without leaks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature branch + unit tests + microbench (ETA 1 week).
Phase 2 (internal canary): deploy to dev cluster, enable for 5% traffic for 48h, collect telemetry and flamegraphs (ETA 1 week).
Phase 3 (staged): enable for 25% traffic with model families that were previously flaky for 72h. Run side-by-side shadow replay to verify checksum behavior (ETA 1 week).
Phase 4 (global): roll to 100% after 7d stable; add runtime config toggle and docs in Console release notes (runtime-2.3 GA).
rollback_plan: Runtime toggle to immediately disable journaled checkpointing per-region and per-customer.
Automatic revert: if replay-abort rate > 0.1% sustained for 1h in production, auto-disable and open incident linking this ticket.
Manual rollback: revert PR that introduced conservative kernel reservation if it causes larger-than-expected perf regression.
metrics: replay_abort_rate: target <= 0.01% in canary, <= 0.1% threshold for auto-disable
